transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-05 10:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Sofia Li (Redwood CSM), Rajesh Kumar (BlueWave Eng Lead), Lena Park (BlueWave Cloud Infra), Samir Bose (BlueWave Security), Maya Ortiz (BlueWave Data Platform)

[00:00] Ava Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off, this is the weekly poc sync for the private vpc pilot for bluewave. quick agenda, networking/routing, kernel and runtime upgrade plan, tuning results, and actions. miguel do you want to start with the current infra items?
[01:12] Miguel Torres: yeah sure, thanks ava. so last week we saw two main issues: one, a subnet routing mismatch where some of the worker nodes couldn't reach the control plane egress; and two, a missed rule on the NACLs that was dropping ephemeral ports during kv cache prefetch. we got logs from the nodes showing tcp resets at around 10k ports.
[02:05] Lena Park: yeah that was us, we had an older baseline terraform module. i updated the sg but i didn't touch the nacl, sorry.
[02:20] Rajesh Kumar: no problem, lena. just to add, our initial benchmark was with seq len 512 and it looked decent, but when we increased to 1024 the latency tail spiked, which we think is due to kernel clock source and also the current quantization path.
[03:05] Miguel Torres: mhm, we suspected that. the runtime's kernel selection for the attention kernel is suboptimal on that driver version. if you upgrade to the 520-ish nvidia driver and the patched kernel we recommended, we should see the tail latency improve 15-30% for long sequences. caveat: the upgrade requires a short interruption and a validated maintenance window.
[04:10] Samir Bose: from security side, we need the firewall checklist and the control plane mTLS cert rotation steps. also need confirmation on where logs are retained and for how long — we've got compliance to satisfy.
[04:48] Sofia Li: we'll attach the retention config and a redwood audit excerpt. ava will also share an excerpt of our SOC2 for reference.
[05:12] Ava Chen: yep i'll send that. miguel, can you also put together the exact ip ranges and ports we need open for the egress to the model workers and the grpc endpoints?
[05:30] Miguel Torres: sure i'll compile a one-pager.
[06:00] Maya Ortiz: quick question about kv caching — in our last run we saw warmups help a lot for repeat queries, but cold-starts were still expensive. is there a recommended prefetch pattern we should use?
[06:30] Miguel Torres: good question. for chat-style traffic with high prefix reuse, we recommend aggressive prefix caching and a pre-warm job during off-peak. also set your batch window to 25-50ms depending on QPS to trade a touch of latency for throughput. note, too big of a batch window hurts single-request tail.
[07:05] Rajesh Kumar: we tried 50ms and saw higher 95th but lower overall cost — it's a tradeoff we can accept if tail is within SLO.
[07:40] Miguel Torres: exactly. also, on quantization: the current 4-bit profile we tried reduces memory but adds a notch to perplexity for some prompts. we can run mixed-precision for critical routes to balance cost and quality.
[08:20] Samir Bose: is mixed-precision supported in private deployment? any key management implications?
[08:35] Miguel Torres: supported. it doesn't change KMS flow — keys are still customer-managed if you choose KMS integration. the only difference is model artifacts with quantized weights, which you host in the same artifact store. no secrets are embedded.
[09:05] Ava Chen: ok turning to routing, lena, can you confirm whether public egress is NAT gateway or managed egress with explicit routes? we saw some traffic hitting an internet egress path which broke the expected VPC peering rules.
[09:35] Lena Park: currently it's NAT gateway for the subnet group, but we can switch to an egress-only route if needed, though that requires updating route tables in three AZs.
[09:55] Maya Ortiz: downtime concerns?
[10:10] Miguel Torres: small hiccup during the change; recommended to do in a maintenance window with traffic diverted. it should be minutes, not hours, but depends on how you drain the workers.
[11:05] Rajesh Kumar: on the benchmark front, we ran a 10k query set, mixed chat and embeddings. overall p95 was 240ms for seq512, but seq1024 p95 jumped to 620ms. the GPU util stayed high but there were stalls.
[11:45] Miguel Torres: stalls usually means kernel or cuda driver mismatch, or memory thrash with kv cache. one more thing: did you enable prefetch concurrency? with kv we prefer 4-8 prefetch threads per node.
[12:15] Maya Ortiz: we used 2 threads. we'll bump to 6 in the next run.
[12:30] Ava Chen: good. next, kernel/runtime upgrade plan — miguel, what windows are you recommending?
[12:50] Miguel Torres: tentatively week of 11/15. steps: snapshot current nodes, apply driver 520+, apply kernel patch, restart runtime, run smoke tests, then run scaled benchmark. we estimate a 20-30 minute interruption per node but we'll do rolling restarts. need signoff from bluewave on the window.
[13:35] Samir Bose: security needs a rollback plan and proof of success criteria; also need to know whether driver update affects auditor tooling.
[13:55] Miguel Torres: rollback is just restore snapshot and reverse driver. we'll document success criteria: p95 within 20% of baseline for seq512 and p95 improved for seq1024. we'll also collect kernel-level metrics and tarball logs for auditors.
[14:30] Rajesh Kumar: sounds reasonable. can you share the smoke test script?
[14:40] Miguel Torres: yes i'll push it to the shared drive.
[15:05] Sofia Li: quick note on procurement: ava i'll follow up on the pilot consumption numbers vs the committed dedicated capacity for next quarter — might be an op to convert to dedicated if their sustained QPS stays high.
[15:30] Ava Chen: makes sense, we'll capture that after the extended benchmarks.
[16:00] Lena Park: one more networking detail — egress IPs for the model nodes changed after the last config; we need a static mapping for our security team. can redwood provide static egress ranges or do we need to pick from our NAT pool?
[16:25] Miguel Torres: for private deployments, you control egress ranges; we can recommend a minimal set of CIDRs for the control plane, but we don't reserve IPs in your VPC. we'll provide the suggested ranges and a small script to lock routes.
[16:50] Samir Bose: ok please send the script.
[17:05] Miguel Torres: will do.
[17:30] Maya Ortiz: regarding metrics, can we get token-level cost and latency breakdown per route in the private console?
[17:45] Ava Chen: yes that's part of the console we shipped — for private you'll get token-level breakdown and per-model dashboards, though retention is configurable. we'll share a demo link.
[18:10] Rajesh Kumar: excellent. any blockers on security docs?
[18:20] Sofia Li: we'll share the SOC2 excerpt and the private deployment compliance pack; samir please let us know if you need anything else.
[18:35] Samir Bose: i'll review and send comments by the 12th.
[19:00] Ava Chen: OK, to recap action items: miguel will send kernel checklist and smoke scripts; i will send SOC2 excerpt and pricing; lena will snapshot and share nacl/sg configs; maya will run the extended benchmark with 6 prefetch threads and upload results; samir will review compliance pack. we'll meet again 2025-11-13 to review results.
[20:10] Rajesh Kumar: thanks everyone.
[20:20] (end of recording)
